data.claim: A width-bounded text renderer over the perf Report data layer renders an empty report as named not-collected sections (never a blank string or a fabricated zero), keeps every line within the width bound, and a figure under the sample floor is n/a.
data.falsifier: render(Report()) returns '' or a line longer than width, or a gate row shows 0s for a missing section.
data.mechanism: sparkline/bar return ''/'n/a' for missing input; render() names not_collected with its task and clips every line to width; the sample floor is carried from stat().
data.question: Does a text renderer of the perf Report render empty data honestly and keep its width bound?

evidence.note: research Rb15f085998 CONFIRMED: run the probe on tests/test_perf_render_text.py -- 8 passed; the empty report renders named not-collected and every line stays within width 20/40/76; sparkline([])=="" and bar(None)=="n/a".

ddflow brief read r-reuse-core, r-small-files, r-everything-configurable, r-no-shell, r-tell-dont-discover, r-unavailable-not-zero, D-no-duckdb, D-sched-no-daemon. render_text extends the report data layer, deterministic, one renderer, samples under the floor are n/a never zero.

ddflow/services/perf/render_text.py (render/to_json/sparkline/bar over Report; reuses metrics.render dur+pct), tests/test_perf_render_text.py (8 tests: width limits, empty data, sparkline/bar degenerate input).

chunk_findings.detail: `sparkline` does not scale to `width` unless every finite value is identical. For `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]` and `width=2` it returns five glyphs (`▁▂▄▆█`), not two cells, so a caller that trusts the docstring and the terminal width bound gets an over-wide line. The same path also drops `None` (`[1.0, None, 3.0]` becomes two blocks), so a missing sample disappears instead of staying unavailable. Only the flat case uses `width` (`_SPARK[0] * width`).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/render_text.py:sparkline

chunk_findings.detail: An empty comparison is still emitted as a header with no rows and no `n/a` / `not collected`. Given `comparisons` of `{"models": [], "reviewers": [], "agents": []}` (or missing keys, which `.get` turns into `[]`), `render` always appends `model        pass`, `reviewer        pass`, and `agent        pass`. That is an empty section, which this module’s own contract says must not be rendered as a blank table.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/render_text.py:_comparison

chunk_findings.detail: There is no size knob, stated cut, or next call. `render` walks every gate and every comparison row; 1000 gates produce 1000 table lines plus headers, with only per-line ellipsis from `_clip`. Nothing records that the answer was cut or names the CLI/MCP call for the rest. `sparkline` is also never used, so the report text has no trend sparkline at all. `_clip` itself is not a bound for `width < 2`: `width=0` and `"abc"` yields `"ab…"` (length 3).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/render_text.py:render

chunk_findings.detail: `sparkline` documents a series scaled to `width` cells, but only the constant branch uses `width`. Given `values=[1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]` and `width=2`, line 30 returns four blocks (`▁▃▅█`), not two; `None`s are dropped first, so `[1.0, None, 9.0]` becomes two cells and no longer lines up with the sample index. A flat series of the same length returns `width` lows, so the two branches disagree on length.
chunk_findings.title: sparkline

chunk_findings.detail: An empty gate list still emits a markdown table. Given `report.gates == []`, `_gates` always starts with the header and separator (lines 64–66) and returns that header-only table. The module contract says a section the log cannot support is `n/a` or named `not collected`, never an empty table; this path does the opposite, and `render` always appends it.
chunk_findings.title: _gates

chunk_findings.detail: Width bounding is false for small `width` and destroys the markdown tables the renderer claims to emit. `_clip("hello", 0)` takes the else branch (`len > 0`) and returns `text[:-1] + "…"` (`"hell…"`), length 5, not a 0-column cut. At the default table path, the gate header is 39 characters; `render(..., width=20)` clips it to `| gate | n | p50 |…`, dropping the closing pipes, so the “markdown table” is not a table. There is also no size cut that states how much was omitted or the next CLI/MCP call to fetch the rest: `render` of any `Report` never names that call.
chunk_findings.title: _clip

chunk_findings.detail: The width-bucketing half of the earlier sparkline finding is fixed, but the unavailable-sample half is not: `xs = [v for v in values if v is not None]` still drops gaps instead of keeping them unavailable. Given `[1.0, None, 3.0]` and `width=20`, the function returns two glyphs, and `_headline` then plots that collapsed series as `gate p90`. A missing p90 disappears from the trend rather than staying a gap, which is the same defect as before (the docstring now describes the drop; it does not fix it).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/render_text.py:sparkline

chunk_findings.detail: Gates now stop at `max_rows` and say how many were cut, but the rest of the earlier bound/next-call finding still holds. `_comparison` still appends every model, reviewer, and agent row with no cut line, so 1000 comparison rows become 1000 lines. The only “next call” text is `to_json for all` / `to_json(report) (the report action's json form)`, which is not an exact CLI command or MCP action name for the remainder [r-tell-dont-discover].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/render_text.py:render

chunk_findings.detail: An uncollected cycle is printed as zero. `report.cycle.get('n', 0)` on `cycle={}` yields `cycle  n=0  p50 …  p90 …` before any `not collected` section. That records a probe that did not run as zero samples, which this change’s own contract forbids.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/render_text.py:render

chunk_findings.detail: The headline sparkline is not a time trend, so it cannot show what got slower or faster. `p90s` is built by sorting `report.gates` on `r["gate"]` (name), then plotted as `gate p90`. Given gates `[("z-old", p90=1.0), ("a-new", p90=9.0)]`, the line is a rising sparkline even if the only change over time was a speedup; alphabetical order is not a before/after series.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/perf/render_text.py:60

chunk_findings.detail: The prior width-clip defect still holds for any positive width shorter than a table row. `_clip` still cuts by character and drops the closing pipes: the gate header is 39 characters, so `render(..., width=20)` yields `| gate | n | p50 |…`, which is not a markdown table. The same clip eats the new omission line, so `width=12` with more gates than `max_rows` turns `… and N more gates (to_json for all)` into a fragment that no longer states the cut or the follow-up call. `width <= 0` is now empty, which does not fix this path (`render` also forces `width` to at least 1).
